decisionMemo.businessProblem: A heavily indebted contractor near covenant breach wants to take on new debt and bid aggressively low to win a large new contract and trade through the hole.

rootCauseDiagnosis.description: Debt / solvency pressure from leverage, covenant, or maturity structure
rootCauseDiagnosis.mechanismDescription: The cash drain is balance-sheet structural — leverage, covenant headroom, interest burden, or a maturity wall — rather than an operating cash problem.
alternativeExplanations: A timing issue on operating cash rather than debt structure
Refinancing already secured that relieves the maturity
missingEvidenceFor: Full debt schedule and covenant test dates

intervention.title: Build a covenant and debt-service model and a proactive lender engagement plan
intervention.objective: Map covenant headroom, debt-service coverage, and the refinancing window before any financing decision
intervention.rationale: A covenant/debt-service model and lender engagement are analysis-only and reversible, confirming the covenant exposure and refinancing window before any financing decision.
intervention.whyThisNow: The pressure is structural; the debt-service position must be modelled before any financing decision

steps.title: Model covenants, debt service, and refinancing window
steps.description: Build a covenant and debt-service model against the next covenant test dates and the refinancing window.
steps.successCriteria: Covenant headroom and debt-service coverage modelled to the next test date

steps.title: Prepare a proactive lender engagement plan
steps.description: Draft a lender engagement and waiver-or-refinancing plan ahead of the next covenant test date.
steps.successCriteria: Lender engagement plan ready ahead of the test date

failureRisks: Lender appetite for a waiver is uncertain
intervention.fallbackPlan: Engage a restructuring advisor if lenders decline a waiver

factors.rationale: Expected revenue impact: MINOR. Urgency: CRITICAL
Duration: 9 days. Team capacity: HIGH. Cost: LOW
Failure risks: 1. Fallback plan available: Yes
Cost band: LOW vs Expected impact: MINOR

recommendedInterventions.sequencingReason: Critical revenue urgency requires immediate stabilization

scenarios.name: Aggressive Recovery (Best Case)
scenarios.description: Execute all interventions in optimal sequence with full team commitment
assumptions: Team capacity fully available (no other initiatives)
Client budget approved for all recommended interventions
No external market shocks during implementation
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Revenue recovery within 90 days, competitive positioning restored
risks: Cascading failures if one intervention stumbles

scenarios.name: Staged Implementation (Recommended)
scenarios.description: Execute top 3 prioritized interventions sequentially, measure, then decide on next wave
assumptions: Top 3 interventions address critical path to revenue recovery
Team capacity for 1-2 major initiatives at a time
Monthly review gates to assess progress and adjust
scenarios.expectedOutcome: Measurable improvement in 60 days, foundation for growth set
risks: Slower overall recovery than aggressive path
Competitors may advance while we execute gradually

limitations: Evidence gaps limit precision: Critical gap: No evidence on Customer Retention; Weak evidence on Operational Efficiency - diagnosis confidence limited; Critical gap: No evidence on Quality Delivery
Evidence coverage is insufficient across business dimensions. Deeper investigation recommended before diagnosis finalization.
nextReviewTriggers: After first intervention completion: validate assumptions, collect outcome data
Monthly: Track KPIs (repeat customer rate, turnaround time, complaint count)
If revenue does not improve by 20% within 60 days: pivot to alternative diagnosis
If team capacity exhausted: pause non-critical interventions
If external market changes significantly: reassess competitive positioning
